favourite.heading: Why West Virginia can pull away
bullets: West Virginia is the better football team by 4.2 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 74% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+4.2 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Oklahoma State can keep it close
bullets: Stylistically the matchup favours Oklahoma State by 0.5 points: ball control vs front disruption (-0.5 pts).
The outcome range is 15.3 points wide at one sigma — p10 -15.2 to p90 +28.8 for West Virginia, so a projection of +7.8 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 4%.
College ratings are built on twelve-game seasons against wildly uneven schedules; even a clean rating gap carries more estimation error than the number implies.
